aliases.name: The Halt Incident
aliases.meaning: after Lt. Col. Charles Halt, principal U.S. military witness

description.summary: A series of reported sightings of unexplained lights and a possible craft over three nights in late December 1980 by U.S. Air Force personnel near the twin NATO bases of RAF Bentwaters and RAF Woodbridge in Suffolk, England.
description.full: The Rendlesham Forest Incident is the most famous British UFO case. Over the nights of 26–28 December 1980, security personnel from the U.S. Air Force units stationed at RAF Bentwaters and RAF Woodbridge — both used by the United States under NATO arrangements — reported unexplained lights descending into Rendlesham Forest, an apparent metallic object on the forest floor, and the return of lights on a subsequent night, during which the deputy base commander, Lt. Col. Charles I. Halt, recorded an audio cassette of the events as they unfolded. Halt's memorandum to the British Ministry of Defence, dated 13 January 1981 and headed 'Unexplained Lights', was released in 1983 under the U.S. Freedom of Information Act and remains the central documentary record. Skeptical investigations have attributed the lights to the Orford Ness lighthouse, a bright fireball meteor that night, and bright stars; some elements remain disputed. The MoD has stated that the case posed no threat to UK national security.

etymology.origin: Rendlesham Forest, the area of forestry between RAF Bentwaters and RAF Woodbridge in Suffolk, where the events took place.
etymology.meaning: Rendlesham is an Old English place-name; the incident is named for the location.
etymology.first_use: Used in print from the early 1980s in UK UFO reports following declassification of the Halt memo.

features.description: In Sergeant Jim Penniston's later account, the object on the forest floor was a small triangular craft with smooth black-glass surfaces and inscribed symbols

features.feature: Pulsing red and blue-green lights (Halt account)
features.description: Halt's audio cassette describes a pulsing red light and additional lights to the north and south on the night of 27/28 December
Halt's memo describes a light 'pencil-like' beamed down into the airfield's weapons storage area

physical.morphology: Reports describe a small (allegedly ~3 m), triangular or domed metallic craft on the first night, and luminous airborne phenomena on the subsequent night.

habitat_preference: forest clearing adjacent to NATO airbase
patterns: Lights observed descending into forest in the early morning of 26 December 1980
Trace impressions and broken branches reported at the supposed landing site
Lights reported returning on the night of 27/28 December 1980, recorded by Halt

range.description: Single localised incident in Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk, England, between RAF Woodbridge and RAF Bentwaters.

hotspots.name: Rendlesham Forest UFO trail

hotspots.notes: The Forestry Commission has installed an interpretive UFO trail with markers indicating the principal locations described in the Halt memo and witness accounts.

hotspots.name: RAF Bentwaters / RAF Woodbridge complex

peak_activity_periods.description: The three nights of reported activity

origins.cultural_roots: Cold War-era UFO interest in NATO-associated military bases in the UK; UK UFO press of the late 1970s and early 1980s.
origins.earliest_accounts: USAF security personnel reports filed in late December 1980; the Halt memorandum to the UK MoD (13 January 1981); the audio cassette recorded by Halt on 27/28 December 1980.
origins.folklore_connections: Linked in popular discussion to Roswell and to other Cold War military UFO claims.

timeline.event: Approx. 03:00: USAF security patrol from RAF Woodbridge East Gate observes lights descending into Rendlesham Forest. Sergeant Jim Penniston, Airman John Burroughs, and Airman Edward Cabansag investigate
Penniston later claimed to have approached and touched a small triangular craft with smooth surfaces and inscribed symbols (an account he developed in subsequent decades)
timeline.significance: Most disputed element of the case
timeline.source: Penniston, J. (later witness statements and books)

timeline.event: Three small impressions and burn marks discovered on the forest floor and photographed; broken branches noted

Night of 27/28 December: Lt. Col. Charles I. Halt leads a small team into the forest, takes radiation readings (claimed peaks ~0.1 mR/h at the impressions), and records 18 minutes of audio cassette describing pulsing red light and other lights to the north and south
timeline.significance: Halt's audio recording is the central primary source

timeline.event: Halt writes a one-page memorandum, 'Unexplained Lights', to the UK Ministry of Defence (RAF Squadron Leader Donald Moreland)
The Halt memo is obtained under the U.S. Freedom of Information Act and published, leading to widespread media coverage in the UK
UK MoD opens its 'Rendlesham File' (DEFE 24/1948) at the National Archives, with progressive releases through 2010
MoD releases its closing 'X-Files' batch including remaining Rendlesham material
timeline.significance: End of MoD UFO project releases

history.modern_era: The case is the subject of dozens of books and television documentaries. Sceptic Ian Ridpath proposed in 1985 that the lights were the Orford Ness lighthouse and a bright fireball that traversed southern England at the relevant time on 26 December 1980; this remains the principal sceptical explanation. Penniston's claim of inscribed symbols and 'binary code' from the craft has been promoted in later books but is not supported by his contemporaneous statement.

notable.name: First night: East Gate sighting and 'craft on the ground' (26 December 1980)

location.description: Forest east of RAF Woodbridge East Gate, Rendlesham Forest, Suffolk

notable.description: In the early hours of 26 December 1980, USAF security personnel at RAF Woodbridge's East Gate reported lights descending into the forest. A patrol entered the forest and according to their statements observed an unidentified object. Penniston subsequently claimed to have approached a small, triangular craft with smooth black surfaces; this account is more developed in his later writings than in his original written statement.
evidence: Photographs of impressions and broken branches taken later that day

factors: Discrepancies between contemporaneous and later witness accounts (especially Penniston)
Skeptical attribution of the descending light to a fireball meteor and the Orford Ness lighthouse
credibility.notes: The Penniston 'craft on the ground' account is the most disputed element.

sources: Witness statements held in MoD files
Ridpath, I. (1985), 'The Rendlesham Forest UFO Case'

notable.name: Halt night: lights and tape recording (27/28 December 1980)

location.description: Forest east of RAF Woodbridge East Gate; Halt and team also describe lights to the north and south

types: Lt. Col. Charles I. Halt (deputy base commander)
USAF security personnel (Bruce Englund, Monroe Nevels, Robert Ball, Adrian Bustinza)

notable.description: On the night of 27/28 December 1980, deputy base commander Lt. Col. Charles Halt entered the forest with a small team and recorded an audio cassette describing impressions in the ground, broken branches, elevated radiation readings (claimed peaks of around 0.1 milliroentgen per hour at the impressions versus background of 0.03–0.04), and a series of lights — including a pulsing red light to the east and lights to the north and south — over a period of about an hour and a half.
evidence: Photographs and plaster casts of ground impressions (now lost or low quality)

factors: Senior officer witness with audio recording
Skeptical attribution to Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees on a five-second flash) and bright stars
Radiation readings disputed as background-level for the area
credibility.notes: Considered the strongest documented portion of the case because of the Halt audio and memo.

sources: Halt memo to MoD (13 January 1981), DEFE 24/1948

physical.name: Three small ground impressions in the forest
physical.description: Three roughly triangular depressions in the forest floor, ~7 inches across, with broken branches around them. Plaster casts are described in the Halt memo.
physical.location: Forest east of RAF Woodbridge East Gate
physical.analysis: Local police were called to the site and noted the marks were consistent with rabbit diggings or animal activity; the Halt memo describes them as having been made by an object on three legs.

physical.name: Geiger counter readings at impressions
physical.description: Halt's team recorded readings of approximately 0.1 milliroentgen per hour at the impressions, against a background of about 0.03–0.04 elsewhere.
physical.analysis: Critics including Ian Ridpath note the readings are within natural background variation in the area and not a meaningful anomaly.

audio.name: Halt audio cassette
audio.description: Approximately 18 minutes of audio recorded by Lt. Col. Charles Halt during the second-night excursion into the forest.
audio.analysis: The recording is genuine and contemporaneous; what it depicts is disputed. Halt narrates a pulsing red light and additional lights to the north and south.

documentary.name: Halt memo: 'Unexplained Lights' (13 January 1981)
documentary.description: One-page memorandum from Lt. Col. Charles I. Halt, USAF, to RAF Squadron Leader Donald Moreland (UK MoD), summarising the events of 26–28 December 1980.
documentary.analysis: Released in 1983 under the U.S. Freedom of Information Act; original held in MoD file DEFE 24/1948 at the UK National Archives.

documentary.name: UK MoD Rendlesham file (DEFE 24/1948)
documentary.description: Ministry of Defence file on the Rendlesham incident, opened to the public at the UK National Archives in stages from 2001.

paranormal.name: Extraterrestrial / non-human craft
paranormal.description: An extraterrestrial or otherwise non-human craft landed (or made low-level passes) in Rendlesham Forest on 26 December 1980, with returning craft on the night of 27/28 December.
evidence_cited: Penniston's account of a small triangular craft

skeptical.name: Lighthouse, fireball, and stars
skeptical.description: The principal sceptical explanation, advanced by Ian Ridpath in 1985, attributes the first-night descending light to a bright fireball meteor over southern England at approximately 02:50 GMT on 26 December 1980, the recurring pulsing light to the Orford Ness lighthouse (visible through the trees on a five-second flash and on the bearing described by Halt), and other lights to bright stars (Sirius, Vega, Deneb).
evidence_cited: Confirmed bright fireball over southern England at 02:50 GMT on 26 December 1980
Geometry of the Orford Ness lighthouse relative to the East Gate
Stellar positions for the time and date

skeptical.name: Misperception under stress and after-the-fact narrative drift
skeptical.description: Independent of the lights themselves, the more dramatic elements (Penniston's craft, inscribed symbols, 'binary code') are products of after-the-fact narrative drift in witness accounts over decades.
evidence_cited: Discrepancies between Penniston's contemporaneous statements and later books
MoD investigation finding no defence significance

stories: The Halt memo and audio cassette
Penniston's claim of inscribed symbols and 'binary code'
folklore.beliefs: Within the UK UFO community, treated as the most important UK case; within mainstream investigation, treated as a misperception case with sociological interest.
